name: Anaerobic digester cooking
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Cooking technologies,Biofuels
description: Renewable based stove - fuelled with biogas from anaerobic digestion.The digestion can take place in a bag or tank which also stores the gas.Anaerobic digestion is an important technology to spread access to clean cooking.
NZErationale: Compared to traditional food stoves, biogas reduces carbon emissions, and compared to use of solid fuels, improves indoor air quality. Light bag stoves may have lower costs compared to other digesters.

name: Biomass gasification stove
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Cooking technologies,Biofuels
description: A biomass gasification stove gasifies solid biomass, such as wood or crop residues, into a combustible gas which is then used for cooking. This process is cleaner and more efficient than burning the solid biomass directly.
NZErationale: Affordable and scalable fuel-efficient cookstoves that can provide several health benefits compared to open fire cooking or inefficient solid cooking stoves.

name: Improved biomass cooking stove
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Cooking technologies,Biofuels
description: Also called rocket stoves, these are fuel-efficient stoves which use biomass, combusting into a well-insulated vertical chimney.
NZErationale: Affordable and scalable fuel-efficient cookstoves that can provide several health benefits compared to open fire cooking or inefficient solid cooking stoves.

name: Electric stove
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Cooking technologies,Electricity
description: Vitroceramic or hot plate stove with an integrated electric resistance providing heat for cooking.
NZErationale: No impact on indoor air quality.

name: Induction cooking
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Cooking technologies,Electricity
description: Cooking equipment which relies on the principle of magnetic induction.
NZErationale: High efficiency,  regardless of the cookware size. No impact on indoor air quality.

name: Hydrogen cooking
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Cooking technologies,Other sources
description: Cooking with hydrogen as the source of heat.
NZErationale: Could act as a replacement of fossil gas in cities that rely heavily on gas for cooking.Also provides access to clean cooking since hydrogen can be produced off-grid in areas with low access to other energy infrastructure.

name: LPG stove
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Cooking technologies,Other sources
description: Cooking stove fuelled by Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG).
NZErationale: Affordable and scalable fuel-efficient cookstoves that can provide several health benefits compared to open fire cooking or inefficient solid cooking stoves

name: Solar cooking
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Cooking technologies,Other sources
description: Renewable-based stove that captures and converts solar energy into heat by means of a mirrored surface.
NZErationale: Affordable and scalable fuel-efficient cookstoves that can provide several health benefits compared to open fire cooking or inefficient solid cooking stoves. Higher time compared to traditional cookstoves, might require auxiliary devices.

name: Building design optimization tools
sector: digital and tools,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building design tools
description: Design tools to support building designers in estimating the combined impact of the different technologies during the design phase of a new building or of a building renovation. Such tools allow management of a greater number of alternatives in finding optimal design solutions. Design tools can be used to optimise material choices,  geometry, building orientation for thermal and lighting performance, amongst other things.
NZErationale: Necessary to combine technologies to maximise the performance of the building.

name: Building information modeling (BIM) softwares
sector: digital and tools,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building design tools
description: Building Information Modeling (BIM) software refers to digital tools that create and manage 3D models enriched with data to support the design, construction, and operation of buildings and infrastructure.
NZErationale: Necessary to combine technologies to maximise the performance of the building.Reduces climate impact of construction.

name: Construction site inspection tools
sector: digital and tools,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building design tools
description: Immersive technologies for buildings enabling remote, real-time inspections of 3D virtual replicas of construction sites
NZErationale: Eliminates travel needs for buildings inspections

name: Composite construction
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope materials,Lightweighting
description: Composite construction uses a combination of two or more materials used together in the main structural elements. Examples include buildings which utilise: steel columns with a floor system of reinforced concrete beams; a steel frame system with a concrete core; concrete-encased steel columns; concrete-filled steel tubes; a timber frame with a concrete core, etc.
NZErationale: Composite construction is already dominating the high-rise construction market, and gaining market shares every year.

name: Funicular floor system
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope materials,Lightweighting
description: The funicular floor is a thin concrete element consisting of vaults and optimised stiffening fins. The thickness of the slab and fins is no more than 20 mm, which allows 70% of the concrete to be replaced by low-density insulation materials to improve the thermal performance of the floor.
NZErationale: The funicular floor system uses (on-average) 70% less concrete than a traditional slab and uses no reinforcement. It also has better environmental performance.

name: Thin shelled concrete
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope materials,Lightweighting
description: A thin shelled concrete roof is a sandwich structure integrating buildings elements (e.g. a hydronic radiant heating and cooling system, thin film photovoltaic systems, etc.) while also serving as a lightweighted roof. The thickness of the concrete varies between 3 and 30 cm, and it withstands stress thanks to its specific shape.
NZErationale: More sustainable material compared to plywood.

name: Additive manufacturing for building materials
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope materials,Reducing material losses
description: The introduction of additive manufacturing (or 3D printing) in the precast concrete industry appears to be a viable solution for high repeatability over many concrete pours. 3D printing can be applied directly to the on-site construction process, reducing the environmental impact while exploring new and complicated geometries.
NZErationale: 3D printing could reduce costs related to raw materials and to labour, while being an effective material efficiency strategy (by cutting material demand by 50%).

name: Building prefabrication
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope materials,Reducing material losses
description: Prefabrication refers to the assembly of structural building components in a controlled environment outside of the construction site. The assembled structure is then transported on site to be finalised.
NZErationale: Reduction of material demand and related energy expenses.

name: Extended building materials lifetime
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope materials,Reducing material losses
description: Modular building components include re-configurable systems, and overall systems, networks and designs that allow disassembly so that buildings can meet different needs (e.g. serving as a meeting room, conference room, co-working space, etc) or even be used for different functions (e.g. office space, residential use, etc).
NZErationale: Lifetime extension is the primary source of material savings in the Net Zero Emissions by 2050 Scenario, and making buildings flexible is key to extending their lifespans.

name: Fabric formwork (building envelope)
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope materials,Reducing material losses
description: Fabric formwork allows the design of concrete elements in a flexible way, using a soft formwork than can be shaped according to an optimised layout. It can be used for walls, columns, and elevated slab soffits (an exterior or interior architectural feature, generally the horizontal, aloft underside of any construction element).
NZErationale: Fabric formwork saves on average 35% of concrete compared to conventional rigid wood or steel panel formwork, but is applied in locations where site logistics might be prohibitive or experienced labour less locally available.

name: Pre-casting for building construction and renovation
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope materials,Reducing material losses
description: Precasting is the use of a reusable mould to produce a structural element in a controlled and standardised environment. The precast is then transported to the construction site to be assembled with other structural pieces.
NZErationale: The use of precast concrete parts in the building sector is a practical method to create modular structure at a lower cost, allowing for a wide variety of shapes and designs. This solution could provide efficiency in the use of material, allowing for reduced material use, and also improve construction and operation efficiency. Good material properties, such as thermal insulation and weather resistance, and the possibility to recycle it make the precast concrete a key factor in the development of the building sector.

name: Dynamic glazing â€“ thermochromic fenestration
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Fenestration
description: Passive modification of properties in terms of thermal transmittance, solar heat gains coefficient and visible transmittance due to a change in temperature.
NZErationale: Lower cost compared to electrochromic but lower controllability and versatility.

name: Electrochromic fenestration
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Fenestration
description: Window able to change transmittance, solar heat gain coefficient and visible transmittance, energised by electrical current.
NZErationale: High energy saving potential.

name: Highly insulating window
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Fenestration
description: Window with R-values of R-5/7 achievable thanks to low emissivity coating, multi-panel, well insulated and sealed glazing assemblies, and low conductivity frames.
NZErationale: Broad applicability, high energy savings and improved comfort.

name: Insulation glass coating
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Fenestration
description: Low emissivity film directly applied in the interior side of windows or to the external window frame to allow or prevent heat gains depending on building energy needs.
NZErationale: Broad applicability, cost competitive when mature, and provides improved comfort.

name: Building integrated solar thermal collector (BIST)
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Solar thermal technologies for wall, roof & faÃ§ades
description: Multi-functional energy facade that receives the solar irradiation and converts it into heat energy for the heating/cooling circuits.
NZErationale: Solar thermal technologies deployed in around 400 million dwellings by 2030 in the Net Zero Emissions by 2050 Scenario.  Packaged solutions are needed to bring down costs, enhance efficiency and improve aesthetics for new houses.

name: Transpiring wall-mounted solar heat collectors
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Solar thermal technologies for wall, roof & faÃ§ades
description: Perforated wall panel that draws the air heated by the sun through perforations into a cavity. Heat calories are then driven into the building's ventilation system during cold days, and ejected directly into the atmosphere during warm days.
NZErationale: Reduction of heating demand in commercial buildings, in particular by maximising heat gains: it converts up to 80% of the sunâ€™s radiation into warm air.

name: Trombe wall
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Solar thermal technologies for wall, roof & faÃ§ades
description: Storage and solar heating walls in components with high thermal mass which leads to indirect heat gains. They encompass a range of designs including classic, composite, water, solar trans-wall, fluidised and photovoltaic.
NZErationale: Simple configuration, high energy savings, cost-competitive when mature.

name: Aerogel insulation from silica or carbon
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Wall, roof & faÃ§ade
description: Insulation made with synthetic porous material in which the liquid component of the gel is replaced with gas (aerogel). They can also be used as transparent insulation materials.
NZErationale: Energy savings associated with the very low thermal conductivity of the material.

name: Building envelope air sealing
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Wall, roof & faÃ§ade
description: Systematic sealing of air leakages throughout the building surface (and particularly around cracks, small holes, plumbing, wiring, lighting and ductwork) to reduce heat loss and better control humidity. This needs to be coupled with appropriate ventilation.Technologies: foam, caulk, tape or gaskets.
NZErationale: High energy savings potential at low cost, improved comfort, improved indoor air quality (reduced humidity, dust, pollen, etc) and increased durability (avoided moisture and condensation).

name: Building integrated heat and moisture exchange panel
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Wall, roof & faÃ§ade
description: Achieving a thermal and humidity transfer in heat recovery ventilators by preconditioning the ventilation air in a modular system (while state-of-the art energy recovery ventilators offer low humidity exchange).
NZErationale: Combines benefits of energy savings from ventilation and increased insulation.

name: Building integrated phase change materials
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Wall, roof & faÃ§ade
description: Phase-change materials provide latent heat storage (i.e. at a constant temperature, by changing the material's phase) and are integrated into different building components. They enhance the building's thermal performance as heat losses are reduced.Integration: in concrete, glazing, between structural elements, using insulation wallboards or even combined with building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV).
NZErationale: The integration of phase-change materials enables greater compactness, a reduction in total system costs (through packaging) and the exploitation of synergies from the various functionalities of building components. Today, costs are still prohibitive of greater market uptake.

name: Carbon negative construction material
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Wall, roof & faÃ§ade
description: Carbon-negative construction materials refer to building materials that not only reduce carbon emissions associated with their production and use but actually capture and store more carbon dioxide (CO2) than is emitted, resulting in a net negative carbon footprint.
NZErationale: Resource efficient construction. Carbon sink.

name: Cool roof
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Wall, roof & faÃ§ade
description: Cool roofs are roofs that stay cool by absorbing less of the incoming energy from the sunlight than conventional roofs.This can be achieved through optical and/or thermal properties, for example by painting the roof in a colour which reflects more sunlight.Other methods include for instance designing the roof in such a way that it better disipates heat to the outside environment.
NZErationale: Reduced demand for space cooling, broad applicability.

name: Double skin facade
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Wall, roof & faÃ§ade
description: Multiple layers of air and glazing where the air cavity is ventilated (naturally or mechanically).
NZErationale: Lower energy demand thanks to increased insulation, ventilation, control of solar heat gains and daylight.

name: Dynamic building envelope
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Wall, roof & faÃ§ade
description: Changing envelope functionality in response to the variation of climate conditions and occupant behaviour, using controllable thermal mass, ventilation, shading, heat exchanges, humidity control, etc.
NZErationale: Increased building flexibility and resilience, maximisation of renewable energy savings exploitation, energy savings.

name: Dynamic insulation
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Wall, roof & faÃ§ade
description: Dynamic insulation draws in cool outside through the insulation layer in the building envelope. As the air moves inward through the permeable insulation, it picks up heat that would otherwise be lost.
NZErationale: Heat recovery from channel-pores optimised to recover heat according to the thermal conductivity of the base material. This can reduce the need for mechanical ventilation thus saving energy.

name: Green roof
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Wall, roof & faÃ§ade
description: A Green roof is a roof partially or completelly covered with vegetation. Green roofs provide insulation, reducing demand for heating and cooling. They can be particularily benefitial in urban environments, where they can help manage rain water and create habitatis for biodiversity.
NZErationale: Reduces energy demand for heating and cooling. Increases resilience to extreme weather.

name: Reflective faÃ§ade
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Wall, roof & faÃ§ade
description: A reflective faÃ§ade that reflects a greater part of the incoming sunlight, therefor staying cooler causing the building to require less cooling.This can be achieved by applying highly reflictive paints that provide the same visible colour range as standard products but exploit the infra-red spectrum to reflect a greater part of the solar irradiation spectrum.Other methods include using construction materials that themselves are reflective, such as special cement with extra reflective properties.
NZErationale: Reduced demand for space cooling, broad applicability.

name: Structural insulated panel
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Wall, roof & faÃ§ade
description: Structural insulated panels, oriented-strand board or side of an insulating core.
NZErationale: Rapid construction, reduced dependence on framing contractors, high performance and no thermal bridges.

name: Vacuum insulated panel
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Design and envelope,Building envelope technologies,Wall, roof & faÃ§ade
description: Porous core enclosed by an air-sealed air and vapour barrier that reduces heat conductivity and component thickness.
NZErationale: The thermal resistance of vacuum insulated panels is 5 to 10 times greater compared to other insulation materials at the same level of thickness.

name: Active control systems
sector: digital and tools,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Building energy management systems
description: Active control systems to operate equipment avoiding grid congestions, enhancing flexibility at the system level. Control can be handled directly by the consumer independently, or through automated demand response where instead the system operator broadcasts a demand-response signal to the consumer.
NZErationale: Employing flexibility of electricity demand while delivering financial benefits to consumers.

name: Building energy management software
sector: digital and tools,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Building energy management systems
description: Building energy management software refers to software used to monitor, control and optimize the energy consumption of buildings. They come in different variations, from simple programs that optimizes the operation of a single boiler or heat pump in a building, to enterprise software used to manage multiple buildings.
NZErationale: Increases energy efficiency in buildings.

name: Building integrated photovoltaic systems
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Building energy management systems
description: Photovoltaic systems (e.g. panels, cells or any other product) are integrated in the building skin. Two technologies are in competition: thick crystal products (made from crystalline silicon) and thin-film products (where an active photovoltaic material is placed on a glass or metal substrate).
NZErationale: High electricity generation potential and high cost-competitiveness under PV-friendly regulations. In the Net Zero Emissions by 2050 Scenario, solar PV and wind supply about 40% of building electricity use by 2030.

name: Direct current buildings system
sector: digital and tools,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Building energy management systems
description: Direct Current (DC) Microgrids combine DC power generation from photovoltaic (PV) sources with battery energy storage and can directly power adapted DC loads (e.g. EV charging, lighting, HVAC) without DC/AC conversion, thus making efficiency gains. With additional AC/DC convertors, they can be connected to the grid and/or power common AC loads.
NZErationale: As the conversion from direct current (produced by PV cells) to alternating current (to transport electricity on a long-distance) generates a loss of 4-8%, and that alternating current needs to be converted back to direct current to power appliances, 100% DC systems are a source of efficiency gains, under the assumptions that electricity is produced and consumed locally in microgrids to avoid transport losses.

name: Gamification devices for buildings energy demand management
sector: digital and tools,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Building energy management systems
description: Using game elements and game design techniques, gamification aims to improve customer participation in demand management programmes (e.g. demand response, energy efficiency).
NZErationale: Thermal comfort tailored to consumer's need.

name: Interval-time of use meter
sector: digital and tools,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Building energy management systems
description: Switch connected to an electricity meter turning on in periods of off-peak tariffs (under a time-of-use (TOU) pricing scheme).
NZErationale: Time of Use (TOU) tariffs (static in many cases) give an incentive for customers to shift their load to off-peak hours. Devices such as storage heaters or water heaters can be connected to the meter to automatically turn on/off, reducing peak demand and reducing electricity bills for consumers.

name: Programmable thermostat
sector: digital and tools,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Building energy management systems
description: Programmable thermostat allowing full control schedules for HVAC operation, based on the user's climate control preferences. A smart thermostat goes far beyond relying on a simple schedule that traditional thermostats might rely on, and can include self-learning algorithms, predictive building controls, occupant level controls, and thermal zoning.
NZErationale: Smart thermostats can reduce heating and cooling demand by 20% to 40% depending on building needs and climate conditions, but could also increase energy use from the rebound effect of the multiple services it can provide.

name: Proportional hydraulic control for buildings
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Building energy management systems
description: Interface between a central boiler or district heat circuit and the heating and hot water system of individual apartments, which also deliver temperature control to the building occupants by hydraulic control providing a more stable temperature compared to thermostatic control.
NZErationale: Diffusion is dependent on the distribution of centralised heating systems; provides more stable temperature control when compared to traditional systems.

name: Smart meter
sector: digital and tools,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Building energy management systems
description: Smart meters are electronic devices that record electricity consumption on a hourly basis or more frequently, and report at least daily to utilities. Smart meters are capable of two-way communication, sending time-based pricing information toward the home or demand response commands to devices.
NZErationale: Smart meters can facilitate more dynamic demand response through a number of load control mechanisms, e.g. sending real-time prices to smart appliances and switching on/off some devices.

name: Packaged air conditioners
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Air conditioners
description: Uses vapour compression refrigeration and a refrigerant system to remove heat from a space and provide cooling. All components (evaporator coil, condenser, and compressor) are located in one cabinet, usually placed outside.
NZErationale: Large potential for deployment, driven by rising cooling demand. Possibility to exploit synergies with various thermal needs (heating, cooling), and benefit from technology spillovers. Generally lower efficiencies compared with split air conditioners.

name: Split air conditioners
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Air conditioners
description: Uses vapour compression refrigeration and a refrigerant system to remove heat from a space and provide cooling. Components are split between an outdoor cabinet (condenser and compressor), and indoor cabinet (evaporator coil) and an air handler, which sends the cool air through the duct system.
NZErationale: Large potential for deployment, driven by rising cooling demand. Possibility to exploit synergies with various thermal needs (heating, cooling), and benefit from technology spillovers.

name: Variable refrigerant flow heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Air conditioners
description: A Variable Refrigerant Flow heat pump system is an advanced HVAC technology that varies the refrigerant flow rate to indoor units. This modulation allows the system to meet precise cooling or heating load requirements in different zones of a building, providing individualized comfort control and high energy efficiency. Typically, a single outdoor unit can connect to many indoor units, enabling simultaneous heating and cooling in different zones.
NZErationale: Large potential for deployment, driven by rising cooling demand. Possibility to exploit synergies with various thermal needs (heating, cooling), and benefit from technology spillovers. Generally lower efficiency compared to other heat pumps/air conditioners.

name: Air-to-air heat pumps
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Air-source heat pumps
description: Transfer heat energy from a colder space to a warmer one, providing either heating or cooling (using either outdoor air or indoor air as a source of heat) thanks to vapour compression refrigeration and a refrigerant system. Typically more efficient than electrical resistance heaters, although efficiencies begin dropping significantly with low outside air temperature (below 5Â°C).
NZErationale: Large potential for deployment, driven by rising cooling demand. Possibility to exploit synergies with various thermal needs (heating, cooling), and benefit from technology spillovers.

name: Air-to-water heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Air-source heat pumps
description: Heat pump transferring heat from the outside air to a water-based system, to either provide hot water or to be used for space heating.
NZErationale: Large potential for deployment, driven by rising cooling demand. Possibility to exploit synergies with various thermal needs (heating, cooling, hot water), and benefit from technology spillovers.

name: Exhaust air heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Air-source heat pumps
description: Air-source heat pump using heat recovery either:1. In cooling mode, as the exhaust air from air conditioners can be recycled and used to deliver other energy services, such as water heating.2. In heating mode, as the exhaust heat can be recovered through a heat exchanger between incoming and exhaust air.
NZErationale: High coefficient of performance (COP), heat recovery of 35-95% of waste heat from cooling.

name: Heat pump water heaters
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Air-source heat pumps
description: Heat pump transferring heat from the outside air to a domestic hot water tank.
NZErationale: Large potential for deployment, steered by more stringent energy codes. Possibility to exploit synergies with various thermal needs (heating, cooling, hot water), and benefit from technology spillovers.

name: High-temperature heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Air-source heat pumps
description: Heat pump with heat sink temperatures in the range of 90 Â°C to 160 Â°C, which can be used in some commercial buildings with specific heating needs.
NZErationale: Limited applicability given that heat pumps are more efficient with reduced temperature difference between the cold and hot energy sources.

name: Integrated heat pump with storage for heating and cooling
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Air-source heat pumps
description: Integrated packages providing optimally balanced heating, cooling and storage, combined with a specific control strategy.
NZErationale: While heat pump and storage components have reached high efficiency levels, better integration and control of these components may give a sizeable increase in system performance.

name: Pellet burning stove and boiler
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Building heating from bioenergy
description: Central or individual heating system providing heat and hot water for multiple or individual rooms, automatically (i.e. independently from the loading) and generally using wood pellets, wood chips, chopped logs, cereal plants, or a combination thereof.
NZErationale: Biomass is a low-carbon resource that can be used efficiently for heating in biomass furnaces and boilers. It is used when sustainable supplies are available (taking into consideration competition with other industrial, power generation and construction applications as well).

name: Wood-burning stove
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Building heating from bioenergy
description: Direct combustion of wood in an enclosed metal box which can be opened at the front for loading, for which exhaust fumes go in a chimney (as opposed to open-fires, whose efficiency is much lower).
NZErationale: Wood burning stoves are replaced by more efficient biomass boilers and furnaces.

name: Evaporative cooler
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Evaporative cooling
description: Converts sensible heat to enthalpy of vapour for reducing the system temperature. It can be air-mediated or water-mediated and direct or indirect.
NZErationale: Energy and cost savings. No refrigerants. Deployment is limited to places with low heating and hot water demand (otherwise a net-zero emissions household would need a reversible unit).

name: Evaporative cooling coupled with permeable membrane
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Evaporative cooling
description: Membrane and evaporative cooling as alternative to vapour compression technologies. Independent control of dry bulb temperature and humidity. The membrane acts as barrier to separate moisture from air.
NZErationale: Independent temperature and humidity control, higher efficiency compared to vapour compression cycles. No refrigerants. Compact units.

name: Liquid or solid desiccant evaporative cooling system
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Evaporative cooling
description: Combination of evaporative and desiccant cooling. Independent control of temperature and humidity. The liquid desiccant, or the rotary wheel in case of solid desiccant, absorbs water vapour due to the difference between the partial vapour pressure of the desiccant and the ambient. Operated by both thermal and electric energy. They can be coupled with membrane to avoid the risk of desiccant contamination.
NZErationale: Independent temperature and humidity control. Expected to reduce consumption by 30-90%  (and 80% peak energy) compared to state-of-art most efficient cooling technologies. No refrigerants. Deployment is limited to places with low heating and hot water demand (otherwise a net-zero emissions household would need a reversible unit).

name: Booster heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Ground-source and water-source heat pumps
description: Heat pumps to supply hot water in buildings connected to district heating systems, allowing for lower temperatures in the district heating network. District heat water is used as heat source for the heat pump boosters.
NZErationale: Booster heat pumps enable district heating networks to operate at lower temperatures and reduce heat losses compared to networks based on central heat pumps only, improving the coefficient of performance of the central heat pumps.

name: Water-source heat pump using waste water
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Ground-source and water-source heat pumps
description: Water-source heat pumps using waste waterâ€”often called sewage heat recoveryâ€”are a technology for sustainable building heating and cooling systems. They extract low-grade thermal energy from municipal or building wastewater using specialized heat exchangers and elevate this energy to usable temperatures with heat pumps.
NZErationale: High coefficient of performance (COP) combined with resource efficient use of waste heat.

name: Water-to-water heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Ground-source and water-source heat pumps
description: A water-to-water heat pump is a highly efficient heating and cooling system that uses water as both the heat source and heat sink, making it ideal for hydronic distribution systems in buildings and district-level applications.
NZErationale: Very high performance relative to air-to-air heat pumps, especially in very cold climates where peak heating demand during the winter season can be an issue.

name: Heat exchanger
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Other building heating and cooling technologies
description: Advanced heat exchangers for building-level substations.
NZErationale: New plate design can reduce pressure loss by 35% and improve the heat transfer by 10%.

name: Heat recovery chiller
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Other building heating and cooling technologies
description: Heat recovery chillers are machines used to produce cooled water, where the waste heat generated during the cooling process is put to use for domestic hot water heating or space heating in a building.
NZErationale: Resource efficient method for providing heating

name: Hydrogen boiler
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Other building heating and cooling technologies
description: Boilers using hydrogen as a fuel instead of natural gas.
NZErationale: Despite a relatively low deployment in the Net Zero Emissions by 2050 Scenario, hydrogen boilers provide a heating solution for buildings connected to a 100% hydrogen network.

name: Hybrid heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Other heat pumps technologies
description: Combined electric heat pump with an electrical resistance heater or a gas condensing boiler as back-up systems.
NZErationale: The use of another fuel under extreme weather conditions allows for a reduction of peak electricity demand.A hybrid solution can act as an important stepping stone towards full electrification of heating.

name: Inclined or deep horizontal wells heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Other heat pumps technologies
description: Closed star-shaped geo-energy inclined exchangers (vertical, deviated or deep horizontal), typically going several hundred metres deep and allowing a drastic reduction of the space footprint of geothermal heating.
NZErationale: Similar (very high) performance to a standard ground-source heat pump, but fully scalable and applicable to many building types, including for retrofit applications in urban environments.Applicable for light industry.

name: Membrane heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Other heat pumps technologies
description: Providing cooling and dehumidification (or humidification and heating), membrane heat pumps are characterised by several permeable membranes and a vacuum pump. Separate control of sensible and latent heat.
NZErationale: Demonstrated energy efficiency ratio twice market average for vapour compression systems, low pressure system, water as working fluid.

name: Metal hydride heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Other heat pumps technologies
description: Non-mechanical heat pump, based on adsorption and desorption mechanisms using metal hydrides and hydrogen as a working fluid.
NZErationale: Despite a relatively low deployment in the Net Zero Emissions by 2050 Scenario, hydrogen can be a solution for buildings connected to a 100% hydrogen network.

name: Natural/hydrocarbon refrigerants
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Other heat pumps technologies
description: Heat pump  using a natural refrigerant, such as CO2, propane gas or ammonia (whose global warming potential can be more than 1000 times lower than conventional refrigerants such as R134a or R410a). For heat pump CO2 water heaters, the refrigerant operates in a transcritical cycle (i.e. behaving like a gas but with the density of a liquid), which enhances energy performance.
NZErationale: Many heat pumps use F-gases as refrigerants, which high GWP and other environmental impact if leaked. Replacing F-gases with propane reduces impact on climante and environment considerably

name: Shallow ground-source heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Other heat pumps technologies
description: Heat pump transferring heat to or from the ground to provide cooling or heating, thanks to a ground heat exchanger buried in the ground. More energy-efficient than air-source heat pumps, especially in winter, as the underground temperature does not drop as much as other heat sources like the air or water.
NZErationale: Very high performance relative to air-to-air heat pumps, especially in very cold climates where peak heating demand during the winter season can be an issue.

name: Thermo-acoustic heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Other heat pumps technologies
description: Thermoacoustic heat pumps work by using an acoustic pressure wave to disburse heating or cooling effects, and generally feature a stack, resonator and heat exchangers. Two recent examples are the Equium heat pump, which rather than a compressor uses a patented sound generator at its core, and BlueHeart Energy, which works with two pistons that oscillate at a frequency of 100 Hz in a closed pressure vessel filled with 50 bar helium. Thermoacoustic heat pumps can reportedly reach higher or lower temperatures than conventional heat pumps, and do not require refrigerants.
NZErationale: The thermoacoustic heat pump is a significantly smaller unit with excellent modulating capability and temperature flexibility, and does not require refrigerants.

name: Fuel cell micro-CHP for buildings
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Polygeneration systems
description: Electrochemical device that converts hydrogen into heat and electricity. The more established polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells operate at temperatures up to 80 Â°C, while the less established fuel cells using solid oxide materials can reach temperatures up to 600 - 850 Â°C. May require back-up options for peak heat demand.
NZErationale: High electrical (48-66%) and total efficiency, no emission of pollutants into the atmosphere. Cogeneration

name: Quad-generation (CCHP +)
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Polygeneration systems
description: Quadgeneration systems produce heating, cooling and electricity while simultaneously recovering CO2 from the exhaust gases.
NZErationale: Covers a wide range of potential applications with potential low to zero carbon emissions.

name: Trigeneration (CCHP)
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Polygeneration systems
description: Trigeneration systems produce heating, cooling and electricity.
NZErationale: On-site production of heat and electricity.

name: Barocaloric cooling
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Solid-state equipment cooling
description: Solid state cooling alternative to vapour compression technologies.  Applying an external field (pressure field) under adiabatic conditions leads to temperature increase of the caloric material which correspond to a change of volume. On the contrary, when decreasing adiabatically the external fields, the temperature of the material decreases to lower values compared to the initial one. The barocaloric effect is coupled with other calorific effects manifesting in the same material (multicaloric effect).
NZErationale: Many alternatives are less environmental friendly. Barocaloric solid refrigerants can achieve the same thermal performance as gaseous refrigerants. This is two orders of magnitude higher than any other solids. While best magnetocaloric materials only achieve a 3-degree temperature lift, barocaloric materials alone achieve 40-50 degrees.

name: Elastocaloric cooling
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Solid-state equipment cooling
description: Solid state cooling alternative to vapour compression technologies. Applying an external field (mechanical stress) under adiabatic conditions leads to temperature increase of the caloric material which correspond to a change of pressure. On the contrary, when decreasing adiabatically the external fields, the temperature of the material decreases to lower values compared to the initial one. It exploits the properties of shape-memory alloys to absorb or release heat from its surroundings.
NZErationale: Many alternatives are less environmental friendly, moderate costs and elevated energy density (over 100J/cm3), projected coefficient of performance (COP) of 6 in HVAC applications.

name: Electrocaloric cooling
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Solid-state equipment cooling
description: Solid state cooling alternative to vapour compression technologies. Applying an external field (electric field) under adiabatic conditions leads to temperature increase of the caloric material which corresponds to a change of polarisation. Conversely, when decreasing adiabatically the external fields, the temperature of the material decreases to lower values compared to the initial one.
NZErationale: Many alternatives are less environmental friendly. Compared to magnetocaloric technologies, the electric fields required can be supplied more easily compared with magnetic fields, with higher power densities and compactness. While material efficiency is high and the cycle is thermodynamically reversible, the cycle is not yet suitable for heating and cooling applications.

name: Magnetocaloric cooling
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Solid-state equipment cooling
description: Solid state cooling alternative to vapour compression technologies. Applying an external field (magnetic fields) under adiabatic conditions leads to temperature increase of the caloric material which correspond to a change of magnetisation. On the contrary, when decreasing adiabatically the external fields, the temperature of the material decreases to lower values compared to the initial one. It exploits the properties of ferromagnetic materials to absorb or release heat from its surroundings.
NZErationale: Estimated efficiency 25% higher compared to best available cooling technologies. Magnetocaloric is the most mature solid state technology, however, there are still limitations in permanent magnet applications.

name: Thermoelectric (peltier effect) cooling
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Solid-state equipment cooling
description: Thermoelectric (Peltier effect) cooling is a solid-state method for transferring heat using electricity, wherein applying a direct current across dissimilar conductors results in heat being absorbed on one face (cooling) and released on the other (heating). The module is usually constructed from arrays of semiconductor pellets sandwiched between conductive plates, and is oriented so that the hot side is attached to a heat sink. Efficiency is notably lower than vapor-compression systems and the technology is generally unsuitable for whole-building air conditioning.â€‹
NZErationale: Thermoelectric cooling is widely applied in cooling of electronics, but is less relevant for cooling of buildings.

name: Absorption heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Thermally-driven heat pump
description: Heat pump driven by thermal energy (delivered by steam or by combustion of natural gas, hydrogen or a mixture of both), instead of being driven by electric energy (for mechanical heat pumps). Based on absorption (with a liquid absorption medium) and evaporation of a refrigerant.
NZErationale: Lower efficiencies compared to electric heat pumps, but greater than traditional gas boilers; they can be fuelled by biogas and can integrate solar, geothermal or other heat sources.

name: Adsorption heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Thermally-driven heat pump
description: Heat pump driven by thermal energy (delivered by steam or by combustion of natural gas, hydrogen or a mixture of both), instead of being driven by electric energy (for mechanical heat pumps). Based on adsorption (with a solid adsorption medium) and evaporation of a refrigerant.
NZErationale: Lower efficiencies compared to electric heat pumps, but greater than traditional gas boilers, and they can be fuelled by biogas and can integrate solar, geothermal or other heat sources.

name: High vacuum flat plate collectors heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Thermally-driven heat pump
description: Heat exchanger that uses solar radiation to heat a water-based system, under high vacuum.
NZErationale: Maximum temperature at 350 Â°C; 450 Â°C with focusing mirrors, use of diffuse light.

name: Vuilleumier heat pump
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Heating, cooling and ventilation technologies,Thermally-driven heat pump
description: Thermally driven machine that cyclically compresses and expands a gas between different volumes. It includes both a heat engine and a heat pump.
NZErationale: Coefficient of performance (COP) estimated for heating as 1.6, can potentially work with hydrogen. Helium is used as working fluid.

name: Conventional LED
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Lighting technologies and control systems
description: Light-emitting diodes (LED) use solid state technology to produce a directional and monochromatic light at very high efficiency and long lifetimes compared to traditional incandescent or compact fluorescent light bulbs. To create white light, LED can either use phosphor conversion or (red, green and blue) RGB systems.
NZErationale: High efficiency and long lifetime compared to alternative lighting, and already starting to be cost-competitive with traditional lighting.

name: Direct current lighting
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Lighting technologies and control systems
description: Direct current lighting refers to light-emitting diodes (LED) run on direct current (DC) and able to be connected directly to a DC grid to avoid the AC/DC conversion required with the traditional AC grid.
NZErationale: Possibility to link them directly to PV systems.

name: Fibre-optic daylighting
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Lighting technologies and control systems
description: Fibre optics combined with solar light collectors to transmit daylight in zones usually hard to light in the day, also called "remote source lighting".
NZErationale: Exploitation of daylight.

name: Lighting control system
sector: digital and tools,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Lighting technologies and control systems
description: Advanced daylighting systems include a wide variety of controls to optimise the use of LED systems by avoiding their use when it is not necessary. They are also able to adjust electrical input depending on natural daylight.
NZErationale: LEDs whose power can adjust to natural daylight and turn off when nobody is in a room will help reduce electricity use for lighting (by 20 to 40% depending on people's behaviour, building usage, etc).

name: Organic LED
sector: mass-manufactured,Buildings,Operations and equipment,Lighting technologies and control systems
description: Organic light-emitting diodes (OLED) are a solid state technology that produce a diffuse light source at high efficiency, making them ideal for use in lighting and displays. They can also be produced on flexible substrates, allowing incorporation into furniture and architecture. There are two types of OLEDs, small-molecular and polymer (PLED). The majority of OLEDs today use the small-molecular subtype.
NZErationale: High efficiency and long lifetime compared to alternative lighting.

name: Electrochemical DAC (e-DAC)
sector: large-scale or industrial,Carbon Capture and Storage,CO2 capture,Direct air capture
description: Electrochemical direct air capture (e-DAC) is an emerging technology to capture CO2 from the atmosphere and either use it as a feedstock or store it underground. e-DAC can operate at or near ambient conditions and run entirely on electricity. Pathways under development include membrane electrodialysis, alkaline electrolysis, electro-swing adsorption and cathodic adsorption. These electrochemical approaches have the potential to reach higher capture efficiency and lower energy use than thermal DAC processes, while requiring a smaller land footprint and offering high operational flexibility, allowing CO2 capture to ramp up and down in response to the availability of low-cost renewable power.
NZErationale: DAC can provide carbon removal services when the captured CO2 is stored underground and exceeds the amount of emissions generated to build, install and operate the plant over its lifetime.

name: Liquid DAC (l-DAC)
sector: large-scale or industrial,Carbon Capture and Storage,CO2 capture,Direct air capture
description: Liquid direct air capture (L-DAC) is a technology that aims to capture CO2 from the atmosphere and either use it as a feedstock or store it underground. L-DAC is based on two closed chemical loops. The first loop takes place in a unit called the contactor, which brings atmospheric air into contact with an aqueous basic solution (such as potassium hydroxide), capturing CO2. The second loop releases the captured CO2 from the solution in a series of units operating at high temperature (between 300Â°C and 900Â°C). A large-scale L-DAC plant can capture around 0.5-1 MtCO2/year from the atmosphere. Water top-up may be required depending on local weather conditions.
NZErationale: DAC can provide carbon removal services when the captured CO2 is stored underground and exceeds the amount of emissions generated to build, install and operate the plant over its lifetime.

name: Solid DAC (s-DAC)
sector: large-scale or industrial,Carbon Capture and Storage,CO2 capture,Direct air capture
description: Solid direct air capture (S-DAC) is a technology that aims to capture CO2 from the atmosphere and either use it as a feedstock or store it underground. S-DAC is based on solid adsorbents operating through an adsorption/desorption cycling process. While the adsorption takes place at ambient temperature and pressure, the desorption happens through a temperatureâ€“vacuum swing process, where CO2 is released at low pressure and medium temperature (80-120Â°C). A single adsorption/desorption unit has a capture capacity of several tens of tonnes of CO2 per year and can be used to extract water from the atmosphere where local conditions allow. An S-DAC plant is designed to be modular and can include as many units as needed.
NZErationale: DAC can provide carbon removal services when the captured CO2 is stored underground and exceeds the amount of emissions generated to build, install and operate the plant over its lifetime.

name: CO2 sequestration in inert carbonate materials (mineralisation)
sector: large-scale or industrial,Carbon Capture and Storage,CO2 storage,Mineral storage
description: CO2 from industrial emitters can be used as a raw material in the production of building materials. The most mature applications involve the replacement of water with CO2 during the formation of concrete, called CO2 curing, and the reaction of CO2 with waste materials from power plants or industrial processes (e.g. iron slag, coal fly ash), which would otherwise be stockpiled or stored in landfill, to form construction aggregates (small particulates used in building materials). The CO2 used in building materials is permanently stored in the product. CO2-cured concrete can deliver lower costs compared to conventionally-produced concrete, while building materials from waste and CO2 can be competitive in some cases, as they avoid the cost associated with conventional waste disposal. Producing building materials from waste can be energy intensive, particularly the pre-treatment and post-treatment steps. For structural applications of building materials (e.g. building, bridges, etc.), multi-year trial projects are required to demonstrate safe and environmentally friendly performance.
NZErationale: CO2 sequestration in carbonates can provide a semi-permanent storage option for CO2, perhaps providing an option where geological storage options are limited and potentially providing value by delivering concrete with lower costs. It requires capture technologies to function and thus achieve emission reductions; if the CO2 is sourced from industrial sources other than cement, it would not reduce the CO2 emissions from cement production itself. The potential for CO2 emissions sequestration can vary considerably according to the mineralisation process employed.

name: Dissolved CO2 injections
sector: large-scale or industrial,Carbon Capture and Storage,CO2 storage,Mineral storage
description: Mineral storage, a technology based on injection of CO2 into rock formations with high concentrations of reactive minerals, is under development. Basalts and peridotites are targeted since both are rich with metals that react with CO2 to form carbonate minerals. Experience of this type of storage is very limited, but it can be done either with supercritical CO2 or with CO2 dissolved in water.
NZErationale: CO2 storage is an essential element of the CCUS chain. CCUS is a key technology enabling emissions reductions across the power, industry and fuel transformation sectors. Furthermore, it can deliver negative emissions by removing CO2 from the atmosphere and storing it permanently underground.

name: Supercritical CO2 injections
sector: large-scale or industrial,Carbon Capture and Storage,CO2 storage,Mineral storage
description: Mineral storage, a technology based on injection of CO2 into rock formations with high concentrations of reactive minerals, is under development. Basalts and peridotites are targeted since both are rich with metals that react with CO2 to form carbonate minerals. name: Advanced CO2 storage monitoring technologies
sector: digital and tools,Carbon Capture and Storage,CO2 storage,Other storage technologies
description: Advanced monitoring technologies are improving the ability to track the movement of the CO2 plume within a reservoir, check for leaks, and monitor reservoir pressure. These technologies are an integral part of safe and secure operations of a storage site. How they are deployed is in part determined by regulatory requirements within a jurisdiction and the specific characteristics of storage sites.
NZErationale: CO2 storage is an essential element of the CCUS chain. CCUS is a key technology enabling emissions reductions across the power, industry and fuel transformation sectors. Furthermore, it can deliver negative emissions by removing CO2 from the atmosphere and storing it permanently underground.

name: CO2 storage in depleted oil and gas reservoir
sector: large-scale or industrial,Carbon Capture and Storage,CO2 storage,Other storage technologies
description: CO2 storage involves permanent retention of CO2 in underground geological reservoirs (> 800 metres deep). The main types of geological reservoirs suitable for CO2 storage are deep saline formations and depleted oil and gas reservoirs.
NZErationale: CO2 storage is an essential element of the CCUS chain. CCUS is a key technology enabling emissions reductions across the power, industry and fuel transformation sectors. Furthermore, it can deliver negative emissions by removing CO2 from the atmosphere and storing it permanently underground.

name: CO2 storage in saline formation
sector: large-scale or industrial,Carbon Capture and Storage,CO2 storage,Other storage technologies
description: CO2 storage involves permanent retention of CO2 in underground geological reservoirs (> 800 metres deep). The main types of geological reservoirs suitable for CO2 storage are deep saline formations and depleted oil and gas reservoirs.
NZErationale: CO2 storage is an essential element of the CCUS chain. CCUS is a key technology enabling emissions reductions across the power, industry and fuel transformation sectors. Furthermore, it can deliver negative emissions by removing CO2 from the atmosphere and storing it permanently underground.

name: CO2-enhanced oil recovery
sector: large-scale or industrial,Carbon Capture and Storage,CO2 storage,Other storage technologies
description: CO2 injections can occur during tertiary production at oil fields to enhance oil recovery. Called CO2-EOR, this technique was pioneered in the United States. Following CO2-EOR operations, the majority of injected CO2 may remain permanently trapped in the reservoir where it was injected. However, conventional CO2-EOR operations require additional activities to confirm that injected CO2 remains stored underground. The IEA calls this CO2-EOR+, https://www.iea.org/reports/storing-co2-through-enhanced-oil-recovery
NZErationale: Out of all CO2 utilisation pathways, CO2-EOR uses the highest volume of captured CO2 per year. It has been a historical driver for CCUS deployment due to the revenue stream it generates.

name: CO2 shipping
sector: large-scale or industrial,Carbon Capture and Storage,CO2 transport
description: Shipping can be used as a long-distance transportation method for CO2, offering more flexibility than pipelines over long distances. CO2 can be shipped at low-, medium- and high-pressure conditions depending on the design of the tanker. Low-pressure and medium-pressure conditions are similar to those found in LPG shipping. Shipping can be port-to-port or port-to-offshore. Infrastructure for CO2 liquification, loading and temporary storage of CO2 is required at the port of departure, and similar infrastructure is required at the receiving port in the case of port-to-port shipping. When CO2 is shipped from port to an offshore location, ships need to be able to interface with offshore infrastructure to unload CO2 into temporary storage, or directly inject it into the storage site. The TRL of ship-based transport of CO2 with direct injection is the lowest, followed by port-to-offshore shipping and then port-to-port shipping.
NZErationale: CO2 transport is an essential element of the CCUS chain. Shipping is particularly interesting for long distance transport of relatively small volumes of CO2. It also provides more flexibility compared to pipeline transport. CCUS is a key technology enabling emissions reductions across the power, industry and fuel transformation sectors. Furthermore, it can deliver negative emissions by removing CO2 from the atmosphere and storing it permanently underground.

name: CO2 terminal
sector: large-scale or industrial,Carbon Capture and Storage,CO2 transport
description: CO2 terminals include infrastructure for CO2 liquification, loading and temporary storage of CO2, in order to receive CO2 coming from various emitters and send it out to multiple storage sites using carriers and pipelines.
NZErationale: CO2 terminals are an essential element of complex CCUS value chains, that can help leverage economies of scale, and allow smaller and disperse emitters easier access to CO2 transport and storage infrastructure.

name: CO2 transport pipeline
sector: large-scale or industrial,Carbon Capture and Storage,CO2 transport
description: Pipelines are a cost-effective way to connect sites where CO2 is captured with sites where CO2 is stored or used.  Pipelines are an effective method to transport large volumes of CO2 and, depending on pipeline design, CO2 can be transported in gaseous, liquid, dense-phase, or supercritical forms. Before pipeline transport, CO2 is compressed to increase the density of the CO2, thereby making it easier and less costly to transport. Certain impurities may also be removed depending on the specifications required by pipeline operators.
NZErationale: CO2 transport is an essential element of the CCUS chain. Pipeline transport is often the easiest and most cost effective mode of transport. CCUS is a key technology enabling emissions reductions across the power, industry and fuel transformation sectors. Furthermore, it can deliver negative emissions by removing CO2 from the atmosphere and storing it permanently underground.

name: Automatic battery recycling
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Battery recycling,Pre-processing and disassembly
description: Having machines separating batteries reduces labour costs as well as the risks encountered by workers. This requires complex machines and AI as the heterogeneity of battery design and lack of design for disassembly increases the complexity and is a barrier to this process.

name: EV battery reuse in BESS
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Battery recycling,Pre-processing and disassembly
description: EV batteries reaching the end of their first life can be repurposed for use in home chargers or stationary battery energy storage systems. This approach allows batteries to deliver their full potential before final recycling. However, several challenges remain. These include the lack of standardisation in EV battery design, which complicates disassembly and repurposing; the need for reliable diagnostic tools to assess degradation and remaining lifetime; and technologies to isolate or replace underperforming cells. Additional barriers include the absence of clear insurance and legal frameworks defining responsibilities during second-life use, and the high cost of repackaging EV battery cells, modules or packs for stationary applications. Advances in these areas are essential to make battery reuse as seamless, competitive and dependable as purchasing new batteries, whose costs continue to decline. Competition from new batteries specifically optimised for stationary storage - often cheaper than repurposed EV batteries - could further limit second-life applications. Moreover, the growing second-hand EV market, which can tolerate lower performance, may extend EV battery use in vehicles rather than in stationary systems.
NZErationale: EV battery being repurposed for battery storage installations might extend the life of EV batteries, shifting part of the demand for primary batteries.

name: Battery direct recycling
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Battery recycling,Processing
description: Direct recycling (also called direct regeneration, direct recovery or relithiation-based recycling) aims to recover electrode materials (cathode/anode) and reactivating it, for example by re-lithiation for the cathode, so that it becomes reusable in a new battery. The cathode is the single most valuable components in battery cells, accounting for approximately 30-40% of its production cost (2024 world battery chemistry average). One of the main issues is that this process needs to be tailored for each battery type and requires access to the single electrodes, which is relatively simple for manufacturing scraps but difficult for end of life batteries.
NZErationale: Direct recycling can lower the energy requirement and increase the efficiency of lithium-ion battery recycling.

name: Battery passport
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Battery recycling,Processing
description: The battery passport allows for tracking of a battery from production to end of life. Barcodes on the battery and its components allow for access to information about the battery composition, use and location. This can be useful for establishing the battery carbon footprint,  improving battery tracking and maximising recycling.
NZErationale: Tracking and tracing batteries throughout their lifecycle - from environmental impacts to use and end-of-life - are essential to inform policymakers and the public, and the battery passport can largely support this goal. These tools help reduce negative impacts and maximise benefits of batteries while facilitating their recovery for recycling.

name: Hydrometallurgical battery recycling
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Battery recycling,Processing
description: Hydrometallurgy involves chemical leaching and purification processes to precipitate out individual metal products. Hydrometallurgy can be used to produce battery-grade materials, for instance battery-grade lithium carbonate or nickel  sulphates, or it can be used to produce intermediate products depending on the reagents used and the level of processing implemented. Advanced hydrometallurgical routes are being developed in industry which can recover the graphite; however, these processes are in their infancy compared with recovering lithium, nickel and cobalt. The primary inputs for hydrometallurgy are black mass Recycling of Critical Minerals Outlook for critical minerals recycling or the intermediate products formed from pyrometallurgy; battery cells or modules cannot be used directly. The black mass feedstock typically has restrictions on the impurity level to be used as an input, for instance copper and aluminium.
NZErationale: Hydrometallurgy, alone or combined with pyrometallurgical methods, is the leading technology for recycling lithium-ion batteries. This will be key to reducing primary demand for critical minerals over the long term, particularly from 2035 onwards, when end-of-life battery feedstock is expected to grow rapidly.

name: Pyrometallurgical-smelting for battery recycling
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Battery recycling,Processing
description: Pyrometallurgy is an established technique for metal extraction and purification, which involves smelting the battery or material in a high-temperature oven, recovering a fraction of the metals as a metal alloy and the remainder of the metals as oxides (slag). The primary recoverable metals are in the form of an alloy (for a lithium nickel manganese cobalt oxide [NMC] chemistry including cobalt, nickel and copper) while others are contained in a slag (such as aluminium, lithium and silicon). Therefore, further hydrometallurgy processing is required to recover the individual metals or battery-grade salts. The removal of several key impurities during the pyrometallurgical smelting process, however, can enable simpler and shorter hydrometallurgy processing. Recovering lithium from the slag is possible using hydrometallurgical processes; however, the yield is typically lower than the nickel and cobalt from the alloy. In pyrometallurgy all the carbon from the graphite is burnt and thus cannot be recovered. Pyrometallurgy requires minimal pretreatment, so battery cells, modules and black mass may be used directly as inputs.
NZErationale: Pyrometallurigal, albeit less widely employed than hydrometallurgical methods, is used to recycle lithium-ion batteries, which will be key to reducing primary demand for critical minerals over the long term, particularly from 2035 onwards, when end-of-life battery feedstock is expected to grow rapidly.

name: Use of a pyro/hydro-metallurgy combo for battery recycling
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Battery recycling,Processing
description: The hybrid pyro-hydro recycling process combines high-temperature treatment to safely break down used batteries with chemical refining to recover and purify key metals for reuse. It offers strong safety performance, flexibility for mixed battery types, and high-quality recovered materials. However, it also involves high energy consumption, potential lithium losses, and greater operational complexity and cost.
NZErationale: Hydrometallurgy, alone or combined with pyrometallurgical methods, is the leading technology for recycling lithium-ion batteries. This will be key to reducing primary demand for critical minerals over the long term, particularly from 2035 onwards, when end-of-life battery feedstock is expected to grow rapidly.

name: Cables' copper incineration
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Cable recycling
description: Copper is recovered by burning the cables. The quality of recovered copper is low, and toxic gasses are emitted. Formerly used a lot but it is now forbidden in many countries.

name: Cables' plastic layer removal with high-pressure water
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Cable recycling
description: High-pressure water jets remove the plastic layer surrounding copper cables. This method has the advantage of not generating waste.

name: Chemical recycling of cables
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Cable recycling
description: A leaching solution dissolves the plastic surrounding cables to liberate the copper therein. It is useful for non-uniformly sized cables but produces waste.

name: Mechanical stripping or crushing of cables
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Cable recycling
description: This method strips the plastics off the cables by blades or cables, these parts are then crushed into particles then separated between plastic and copper. It is easy to implement and low cost, and so it is largely adopted, especially in regulated markets limiting or not authorizing the use of cable incineration.

name: Thermal decomposition of cables
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Cable recycling
description: This method consists in placing cables in a warm environment with no oxygen. The plastic degrades into organic fuel which can be recovered. The method is highly efficient and no waste is generated.

name: Cryogenic grinding
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Cross-cutting recycling,Pre-processing and disassembly
description: Freezing helps in grinding elements in a fine dust. Liquid nitrogen is often used to maintain a temperature below -100 degrees Celsius. The so created fine milling is mostly composed of single phase particles, which are easier to recycle.
NZErationale: This method can improve the yield of recycling processes, leading to a better circularity of materials embedded in electronics.

name: Supercritical carbon dioxide uses for metal recovery
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Cross-cutting recycling,Pre-processing and disassembly
description: Instead on relying on acids to leach metals from printed circuits, supercritical CO2 and co-solvents are used to recover metals from complex structures. This method is more rapid and generates less waste compared to acid leaching.

name: Advanced hydrometallurgy in recycling processes
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Cross-cutting recycling,Processing
description: This next-generation leaching and solvent extraction technique is optimised for critical minerals. It relies on selective leaching and advanced separation membranes for improved recovery rate and lowered chemical consumption compared to regular hydrometallurgy.
NZErationale: Hydrometallurgy, alone or combined with pyrometallurgical methods, is the leading technology for recycling lithium-ion batteries. This will be key to reducing primary demand for critical minerals over the long term, particularly from 2035 onwards, when end-of-life battery feedstock is expected to grow rapidly.

name: Biological metals reclamation
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Cross-cutting recycling,Processing
description: This technology makes use of microorganisms to help in the recovery of metals (Li, CO, Cu, Ni, Mn, Al). The efficiency can even be higher than other methods, but the time required is much longer than hydrometallurgical methods. Already in used by the mining industry.
NZErationale: Biological reclamation can enables new sources of critical minerals.

name: Electrochemical recovery systems
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Cross-cutting recycling,Processing
description: Advanced electrowinning and electrorefining processes designed specifically for recovering high-purity metals from complex, low-concentration solutions. This technology applies to secondary and primary metal production.
NZErationale: Electrochemical recovery can increase the recycling efficiency for several metals and materials, including those in lithium-ion batteries.

name: Plasma arc recycling
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Cross-cutting recycling,Processing
description: A plasma arc is used to heat waste at a high temperature to selectively recover targeted elements. This allows for high recovery rate, even for complex feedstock such as electronic waste.

name: Virtual model of the entire recycling process
sector: digital and tools,Critical minerals,E-waste recycling,Cross-cutting recycling,Processing
description: The development of a virtual model of the entire recycling process allows for real-time optimisation and predictive maintenance.

name: Bioleaching
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,Mineral processing and refining,Hydrometallurgy
description: Bioleaching, or biomining, relies on microorganisms to extract metals from low-grade ore. The technology can be used to improve the production of a mine and to reduce pollution by cleaning toxins in mining waste. Today, 15% of copper and 5% of gold is produced thanks to bioleaching.

name: Direct lithium extraction from brine
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,Mineral processing and refining,Hydrometallurgy
description: Direct lithium extraction (DLE) from brine refers to a set of chemical and physical processes used to selectively recover lithium ions directly from natural or produced brines without relying on long-duration solar evaporation ponds. In DLE systems, lithium is captured from the brine using techniques such as adsorption, ion exchange, solvent extraction, membrane-based separation, or selective precipitation, followed by stripping and concentration to produce a lithium-rich solution suitable for further refining into battery-grade lithium chemicals.
NZErationale: The report The Role of Critical Minerals in Clean Energy Transitions (2021, IEA) identified lithium as a mineral needed for batteries and other technologies. Supply to reach net-zero projections is insufficient. Geothermal brines offer a broad supply base supporting domestic energy security. Technology for extraction is in demonstration phases. However, further research to identify scale-up issues (including lack of local processing capabilities) is needed.

name: High pressure acid leaching
sector: large-scale or industrial,Critical minerals,Mineral processing and refining,Hydrometallurgy
